correctness.rationale: For any positive definite M with eigenvalues 1/a²,1/b² and r<b, Vieta gives Q_r(n)=[1−r² nᵀMn]/(vᵀMv)=r²+(1−r² trM)/(vᵀMv). The two extremal values (b²−r²b²/a², a²−r²a²/b²) are ordered by sign of 1−r²trM; the endpoint nearer r² is the first, making λ=(q_far−r²)/(q_near−r²)=a²/b² and b²=q_near+r²/λ. The only noncircular constant case is trM=1/r² and then Q≡r², including circle a=b=√2r. Two distinct s<r cannot both obey the resonance equation. Uniform angular vᵀMv is arcsine; monotone Jacobian yields exactly the stated density, with numerator a positive product of two signed deviations. No finite experiments are used to prove the continuum theorem. Independently checked 320 quadratic products/inversions and three resonance families, including second-radius separation.
